title: Lester Young's birthplace and his love for the black race
summary: Jones says Lester was born in Mississippi, loved the black race more than anyone, and that Jones looked after his affairs and buried him.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: I always thought he was born in New Orleans.

No. It wouldn't have made no difference if he'd been born in Pocatello, Idaho, or Boston, Mass. There has never been - and I'm 61 - there has never been one black man in the world that loved the black race like Lester Young, nobody. I have been now with the Civil Rights leaders. I knew them in their infancy days. I've been involved in 15 or 20 things, but I have never known nobody to love the black race like Lester Young.
What town in Mississippi was he born in?
There are many small towns; do you happen to know the name of it?

It was not too far from Natchez. It was the kind of town that when he was born - you know what they were. The little RFD towns that was then, they were way stops. You know, you got your Rural Delivery and what have you.
I was born in Mississippi, but I know the name of the town.
I wonder how the records will have it?

The records will show, you see, his mother being from New Orleans, and his father. But his passport and everything, even in the Army, and I was there - it's got to say Mississippi, but what town I can't remember. It's a nonentity almost.
Did you ever go to Europe with Lester?
No, I didn't go to Europe with Lester.
I just wondered how you would know about passports.

At that particular time, since I was so close to Lester and since I was relatively close with Norman Granz, I always took care of a lot of things for Les because you must remember, Lester would not go to a doctor or nothing unless he consulted me, because you remember, I buried Lester. His mother, his wife, his sister, and everybody said, 'Jo, you got it,' you see. As I reiterate, there has never been nobody from Marcus Garvey up that ever loved the black man like Lester Young, nobody! Because he was so sensitive, he was so sincere. In the first place he didn't like to see no human being mistreated. You could tell it in his playing.
